Action Plan:
1. Call emergency services (999) for suspected anaphylaxis; patient advised to remain on the line until ambulance arrival.
2. Instruct patient to take any available oral antihistamine immediately while awaiting paramedics.
3. Ensure a responsible adult (patient’s mother) stays with the patient until hand-over to ambulance crew.
4. Post-discharge: arrange follow-up for prescription of adrenaline auto-injector, written anaphylaxis plan, and formal food allergy testing.
5. Review asthma control and consider adding preventive (inhaled corticosteroid) therapy at follow-up.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 23-year-old female presents with rapid-onset upper-lip swelling, difficulty breathing, chest tightness, and dizziness ~30 min after eating prawn soup (onset ~19:00).  
• Symptoms progressively worsening at time of call.  
• Similar episode one year ago after late-night meal (no clear trigger identified).  
• Past medical history: asthma (uses salbutamol inhaler).  
• Known peanut allergy since childhood; required hospital treatment with injection at age 6.  
• Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); intermittent oral antihistamines (names/doses not recalled).  
• Allergies: peanuts (severe); possible shellfish (new suspected trigger).  
• Social: Lives with mother; friend visiting at time of call.

Objective:
• Telehealth consultation—no vital signs obtained.  
• Visual: upper-lip swelling noted by patient (exact size not documented).  
• Patient reports dyspnoea, chest tightness, and dizziness—suggesting systemic reaction.  
• No other physical findings available.  
• No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute allergic reaction / suspected anaphylaxis  
   - Assessment: Likely anaphylaxis to shellfish (prawn).  
   - Investigations: To be performed in ED (e.g., vitals, airway assessment, serum tryptase as per ED protocol).  
   - Treatment: Immediate ambulance dispatch; advice to take oral antihistamine; anticipate IM adrenaline, oxygen, IV fluids, corticosteroids in ED.  
   - Referral: Emergency department now; later referral to allergy clinic for evaluation and provision of adrenaline auto-injector.

2. Asthma  
   - Assessment: Known intermittent asthma; salbutamol only.  
   - Investigations planned: Review peak-flow diary and control score at follow-up.  
   - Treatment planned: Consider inhaled corticosteroid initiation if control sub-optimal; reinforce inhaler technique.  
   - Relevant referrals: None at present; manage in primary care after acute event.

3. Food allergies (peanut, possible shellfish)  
   - Assessment: Confirmed peanut allergy; probable shellfish allergy.  
   - Investigations planned: Formal skin-prick or specific IgE testing after acute phase.  
   - Treatment planned: Education on food avoidance, written allergy action plan, prescription of two adrenaline auto-injectors.  
   - Relevant referrals: Specialist allergy service for comprehensive assessment and desensitisation advice if appropriate.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: Vital signs, full medication list with doses, complete allergy list (drug/latex).  
• No internal transcript conflicts detected.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor background noise but clinical details audible.
